articles.title: Apple blocked over $11 billion in App Store fraud in 6 years
articles.summary: Apple reported preventing over $11 billion in fraudulent App Store transactions over a six-year period, with $2.2 billion blocked in 2025 alone. This disclosure highlights the ongoing challenge of combating financial fraud and illicit activities within digital app marketplaces.

articles.title: UK plans for cybercrime law reform would protect almost no one, experts warn
articles.summary: Experts warn that proposed UK cybercrime law reforms would hinder security researchers by forcing them to halt investigations prematurely upon identifying potential vulnerabilities. This restriction prevents researchers from verifying, assessing, or determining the exploitability of critical security flaws.

articles.title: Attackers are bypassing MFA on SonicWall VPNs because something was wrong with previous fix
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting SonicWall Gen6 VPNs by bypassing MFA, as administrators failed to complete all required manual steps for a previously issued patch. This highlights the critical risk of incomplete remediation processes in security maintenance.

articles.title: Showboat Linux Malware Hits Middle East Telecom with SOCKS5 Proxy Backdoor
articles.summary: The Showboat modular Linux malware has been identified in a long-running campaign targeting Middle Eastern telecommunications infrastructure to establish remote access and SOCKS5 proxy capabilities. Researchers report the framework has been active since at least 2022, facilitating file transfers and shell access for post-exploitation activities.

articles.title: Authorities dismantle First VPN, used by ransomware actors
articles.summary: Law enforcement agencies from France, the Netherlands, and Europol dismantled the First VPN service, which was specifically marketed to and utilized by ransomware actors to maintain anonymity. The operation involved seizing 33 servers and shutting down associated domains to disrupt the infrastructure supporting cybercriminal activities.

articles.title: Inside a Crypto Drainer: How to Spot it Before it Empties Your Wallet
articles.summary: This article examines the operational mechanics of the Lucifer DaaS platform, which facilitates large-scale cryptocurrency theft by tricking users into signing malicious transactions. It provides insights into how modern crypto drainers leverage automation and social engineering to bypass wallet security.

articles.title: Chinese hackers target telcos with new Linux, Windows malware
articles.summary: Chinese state-sponsored actors are targeting telecommunications providers using new, platform-specific malware variants identified as Showboat and JFMBackdoor. These tools are designed to facilitate ongoing cyber-espionage activities against critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Max severity Cisco Secure Workload flaw gives Site Admin privileges
articles.summary: Cisco has issued security updates for a critical vulnerability in Secure Workload that permits unauthenticated attackers to escalate privileges to a Site Admin level.

articles.title: GitHub, Grafana Labs breaches traced back to TanStack supply chain compromise
articles.summary: GitHub and Grafana Labs suffered security breaches after threat group TeamPCP injected malicious code into the popular Nx Console VS Code extension. This supply chain attack allowed attackers to steal credentials, infiltrate CI/CD pipelines, and exfiltrate thousands of private GitHub repositories.

articles.title: Cisco fixed maximum severity flaw CVE-2026-20223 in Secure Workload
articles.summary: Cisco has released patches for a maximum severity (CVSS 10.0) vulnerability in its Secure Workload product, which could allow remote attackers to gain unauthorized Site Admin privileges via crafted API requests.

articles.title: Police seize “First VPN” service used in ransomware, data theft attacks
articles.summary: International law enforcement agencies have shut down 'First VPN,' a service frequently utilized by cybercriminals to facilitate ransomware deployments and data theft operations.

articles.title: Europol Seizes First VPN Used by Ransomware Gangs, Arrests Administrator
articles.summary: Europol has dismantled First VPN, a service frequently exploited by ransomware gangs, resulting in the arrest of its administrator and the seizure of user data. This operation significantly disrupts the infrastructure used by cybercriminals to facilitate malicious activities.

articles.title: Attackers spill plaintext passwords of 46k Myspace93 users after 2021 breach
articles.summary: Approximately 46,000 Myspace93 users had their unencrypted passwords and email addresses exposed following a 2021 data breach. The incident was attributed to unauthorized access through compromised internal connections.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Linux Rootkits, Router 0-Day, AI Intrusions, Scam Kits and 25 New Stories
articles.summary: This bulletin highlights an evolving threat landscape where attackers are increasingly exploiting trusted systems, cloud services, and standard software updates rather than just traditional infiltration methods. The report emphasizes the risk posed by compromised legitimate infrastructure, including AI-driven intrusions and router vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Android Malware Spotted Subscribing Victims to Paid Services Without Consent
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a widespread Android malware campaign that uses deceptive applications to enroll unsuspecting users in paid premium SMS services without their authorization. This long-running operation has impacted users globally by generating unauthorized financial charges.

articles.title: Cisco serves up yet another perfect 10 bug with Secure Workload admin flaw
articles.summary: Cisco has patched a critical vulnerability in its Secure Workload platform that could allow unauthorized actors to access sensitive data and modify configurations across tenant boundaries. This flaw stems from a security issue within internal APIs and carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0.

articles.title: Flipper One project needs community help to build open Linux platform
articles.summary: Flipper Devices is seeking community collaboration to develop Flipper One, an open Linux-based platform aimed at connected device research. This initiative expands the company's ecosystem beyond their existing Flipper Zero pentesting tool.

articles.title: Microsoft Defender vulnerabilities exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-41091, CVE-2026-45498)
articles.summary: Microsoft Defender vulnerabilities CVE-2026-41091 and CVE-2026-45498 are being actively exploited in the wild, with the former allowing local privilege elevation to SYSTEM level. CISA has added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of Two Actively Exploited Defender Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Microsoft has confirmed active exploitation of two vulnerabilities in Microsoft Defender, including a high-severity privilege escalation flaw that grants attackers SYSTEM access. Users are advised to monitor for updates to mitigate these security risks.

articles.title: When Identity is the Attack Path
articles.summary: This article highlights how common, legitimate credential caching behaviors in cloud environments can be exploited by attackers to gain extensive unauthorized access. It emphasizes that standard security configurations may not prevent identity-based attacks that leverage stored keys to compromise critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Microsoft storms RAMPART, adds Clarity to agentic AI safety
articles.summary: Microsoft has open-sourced RAMPART and Clarity, two new tools designed to enhance the security, safety, and evaluation of agentic AI systems. These resources aim to help developers build more resilient agents by providing frameworks for monitoring and testing.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Retired IE Tool MSHTA Now Being Used in Fileless Malware Attacks
articles.summary: Hackers are exploiting the retired MSHTA utility to execute stealthy, fileless malware attacks on Windows systems. This technique persists despite Microsoft's official retirement of Internet Explorer.

articles.title: The readiness paradox: Why a false sense of cyber confidence is becoming a liability
articles.summary: The rise of AI-driven threats and alert fatigue necessitates a shift toward proactive cyber exposure management to address the dangers of overconfidence. Organizations must move beyond a false sense of security to accurately identify and mitigate concentrated risks before they result in a crisis.

articles.title: Virtru centers file collaboration around data-level protection
articles.summary: Virtru has launched Virtru Collaborate, a FedRAMP-authorized platform that utilizes the Trusted Data Format (TDF) to provide persistent, data-level encryption and policy enforcement for secure file collaboration. This solution is the first to be built on the new Virtru Platform architecture, designed to maintain protection as files are shared across organizational boundaries.

articles.title: ASAPP expands adversarial testing for enterprise AI systems
articles.summary: ASAPP has introduced 'Continuous Red Teaming,' a new feature utilizing the Promptfoo platform to conduct automated adversarial testing for AI systems. This initiative aims to detect over 50 types of AI vulnerabilities in real-time to enhance production security and reliability.

articles.title: Tenable Hexa AI automates remediation across attack surfaces
articles.summary: Tenable has launched Hexa AI, an agentic AI engine integrated into the Tenable One Exposure Management Platform to automate vulnerability remediation and risk reduction. The tool utilizes multi-step reasoning and Model Context Protocol support to streamline security workflows and address complex attack surfaces.

articles.title: Microsoft warns of new Defender zero-days exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft has released security patches to address two zero-day vulnerabilities in Microsoft Defender that are currently being exploited by attackers. Users are urged to update their systems to mitigate potential threats.

articles.title: Riverbed introduces new Aternity tools for autonomous IT operations
articles.summary: Riverbed has launched new Aternity capabilities aimed at enabling autonomous IT operations and improving digital experience management through automation and enhanced visibility. The tools are designed to shift IT teams toward proactive, prevention-focused workflows to ensure business continuity.

articles.title: Forward launches Predict to test network changes before deployment
articles.summary: Forward has introduced a new capability called Forward Predict, which utilizes a digital twin of a network to simulate and evaluate the impact of changes before they are deployed to production. This tool aims to enhance network security and stability by identifying potential issues in a pre-deployment environment.

articles.title: 9-Year-Old Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Root Command Execution on Major Distros
articles.summary: A long-standing Linux kernel vulnerability has been discovered that allows unprivileged local users to perform unauthorized privilege escalation and execute commands as root. The flaw has persisted undetected for nine years and affects default installations of major Linux distributions.

articles.title: CTERA brings AI insights and automation for unstructured data
articles.summary: CTERA has launched CTERA InsightAI, an agentic AI intelligence layer designed to enhance data observability by automating the identification of security risks, unusual behaviors, and operational inefficiencies within unstructured data. The platform aims to provide enterprises with real-time insights to better manage and secure large-scale data environments.

articles.title: Terra adds continuous network exploitation validation to its platform
articles.summary: Terra Security has expanded its platform's offensive security capabilities to include continuous network exploitation validation, extending its reach beyond web applications and AI. This new feature allows customers to automatically test the resilience of their network infrastructure against potential exploits.

articles.title: Zombie user account let hackers control the city’s water
articles.summary: Hackers gained unauthorized control over a city's water infrastructure by exploiting a neglected user account that belonged to a former employee. The incident highlights the critical importance of effective offboarding processes to prevent unauthorized access.

articles.title: GitHub links repo breach to TanStack npm supply-chain attack
articles.summary: GitHub confirmed that hackers accessed over 3,800 internal repositories by leveraging a malicious version of the Nx Console VS Code extension, which was compromised through a supply-chain attack on the TanStack npm package. This incident highlights the significant risks posed by compromised developer tools within the software supply chain.

articles.title: Discord adds end-to-end encryption to voice and video calls by default
articles.summary: Discord has implemented end-to-end encryption by default for all voice and video calls, ensuring that conversations remain private and inaccessible to the platform provider. This change was applied automatically to all users without requiring manual configuration or prior notification.

articles.title: GitHub Internal Repositories Breached via Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension
articles.summary: GitHub suffered an internal repository breach after an employee's device was compromised by a malicious version of the Nx Console VS Code extension. The attack originated from a prior compromise of an Nx developer's system.

articles.title: Cyber threats push SMBs to spend more on security
articles.summary: Small and medium-sized businesses are increasing their cybersecurity budgets in response to rising threats and the integration of artificial intelligence. Despite the increased investment, many organizations continue to rely on reactive security measures.

articles.title: Highly Critical Drupal Core Flaw Exposes PostgreSQL Sites to RCE Attacks
articles.summary: Drupal has issued security updates to address a critical vulnerability in its database abstraction API that could allow attackers to execute remote code, escalate privileges, or access sensitive information on PostgreSQL-based sites. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-9082.

articles.title: Europe dismantles VPN service used by cybercriminals to hide ransomware attacks
articles.summary: International law enforcement successfully dismantled First VPN, a service widely used by ransomware operators to obfuscate their activities on criminal forums. The operation aims to disrupt the infrastructure facilitating major cyberattacks.

articles.title: Xi and Putin pledge closer cooperation on AI, cyberspace and satellite systems
articles.summary: Russia and China have announced a strategic partnership to develop independent technological ecosystems in AI, satellite systems, and software to reduce reliance on Western infrastructure. This alignment signals a shift in global technological power dynamics aimed at countering policies from nations deemed unfriendly.

articles.title: Ukraine identifies infostealer operator tied to 28,000 stolen accounts
articles.summary: Ukrainian cyberpolice and U.S. law enforcement have identified an 18-year-old suspect in Odesa for operating an infostealer malware campaign that compromised 28,000 accounts. The operation specifically targeted customers of a California-based online store.

articles.title: Hackers bypass SonicWall VPN MFA due to incomplete patching
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting incomplete patches on SonicWall Gen6 SSL-VPN appliances to brute-force credentials and bypass multi-factor authentication for ransomware deployment. Organizations are urged to ensure their devices are fully updated to mitigate this unauthorized access.

articles.title: Even Claude agrees: hole in its sandbox was real and dangerous
articles.summary: An undisclosed and potentially dangerous sandbox vulnerability in the Claude AI model was identified and silently patched without a formal CVE or public disclosure. The lack of transparency regarding this security flaw highlights concerns about silent remediation practices in AI infrastructure.

articles.title: PinTheft: Another Linux Privilege Escalation, Another Working Exploit, This Time Targeting Arch
articles.summary: PinTheft is a newly identified local privilege escalation vulnerability within the Linux RDS subsystem that currently has publicly available exploit code. Arch Linux users are at the highest risk and are urged to apply patches immediately to mitigate the threat.

articles.title: Meet Rampart and Clarity, Microsoft’s new red team combo AI agents
articles.summary: Microsoft has open-sourced two new AI agents, Rampart and Clarity, designed to assist developers and incident responders in red-teaming security operations. These tools aim to improve automated threat detection and proactive defense testing.

articles.title: The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations (Updated May 20)
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides an updated analysis of the evolving npm supply chain threat landscape, highlighting sophisticated tactics such as wormable malware and CI/CD persistence. The report outlines emerging attack vectors and necessary mitigation strategies for developers and organizations.

articles.title: FTC warns 12 major tech firms of violating Take It Down Act
articles.summary: The FTC has issued warnings to 12 major tech companies regarding their compliance with the Take It Down Act, which requires the removal of nonconsensual intimate images within 48 hours of a request. This action emphasizes the regulatory pressure on platforms to improve user safety and content moderation practices.

articles.title: Microsoft Open-Sources RAMPART and Clarity to Secure AI Agents During Development
articles.summary: Microsoft has released two open-source tools, RAMPART and Clarity, designed to help developers test and secure AI agents against potential security risks. These frameworks facilitate automated safety testing during the AI development lifecycle.

articles.title: Ukraine probes teen suspect in cyber theft scheme targeting California online shoppers
articles.summary: Ukrainian authorities are investigating a teenage suspect linked to a cyber theft scheme targeting online shoppers in California. The case originated from intelligence shared by U.S. officials regarding hackers operating within Ukraine.

articles.title: Discord migrates all users to end-to-end encryption by default
articles.summary: Discord has transitioned all user messaging to default end-to-end encryption, bucking a trend seen in other social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok.

articles.title: 7-Eleven confirms breach after ShinyHunters claims
articles.summary: 7-Eleven confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to systems containing franchisee documents after the ShinyHunters threat group claimed responsibility. The incident was discovered on April 8, prompting an internal investigation into the exposure.

articles.title: Grafana breach caused by missed token rotation after TanStack attack
articles.summary: Grafana experienced a data breach resulting from a failure to rotate a GitHub workflow token following the recent TanStack npm supply-chain attack. The oversight allowed unauthorized access due to a remaining valid credential that should have been revoked.

articles.title: Microsoft issues YellowKey mitigation, no patch yet
articles.summary: Microsoft has released manual mitigations for the YellowKey BitLocker bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-45585) instead of a formal software patch. Users are advised to disable autofstx.exe and enable TPM+PIN to secure their systems.

articles.title: Understanding Trend Structure: Higher Highs and Lower Lows Explained
articles.summary: This article discusses technical market analysis techniques regarding price structure, such as higher highs and lower lows. It does not contain information related to cybersecurity.

articles.title: GitHub says internal repositories were impacted in poisoned VS Code extension attack
articles.summary: GitHub experienced a data breach involving internal repositories after an employee's device was compromised by a malicious Visual Studio Code extension. The incident highlights the escalating security risks associated with third-party developer tools within software development ecosystems.

articles.title: Microsoft Takes Down Malware-Signing Service Behind Ransomware Attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft disrupted a malware-signing-as-a-service operation run by the threat actor Fox Tempest that abused legitimate signing systems to distribute ransomware. The operation impacted thousands of global networks and devices.

articles.title: Webworm APT targets European government organizations with new backdoors
articles.summary: The China-aligned APT group Webworm, also known as Space Pirates, has expanded its cyber espionage operations to target government organizations across Europe and a university in South Africa using new backdoors. The activity was uncovered by ESET, highlighting the group's evolving geographic reach since its inception in 2022.

articles.title: Verizon DBIR: Vulnerability exploitation is the dominant initial access vector
articles.summary: The 2026 Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report reveals that vulnerability exploitation has surpassed stolen credentials as the primary method for initial network access. This shift marks the first time in 19 years that credential theft has not been the leading vector for cyberattacks.

articles.title: Identity Alone Isn't Enough: Why Device Security Has to Share the Load
articles.summary: The headline highlights that identity-based authentication is no longer sufficient to secure networks against modern threats, emphasizing the necessity of integrating continuous device verification within Zero Trust architectures. It notes that attackers are increasingly bypassing identity checks by exploiting compromised devices and stolen session tokens.

articles.title: NanoCo lands $12 million seed funding, launches enterprise assistant built on NanoClaw
articles.summary: NanoCo has secured $12 million in seed funding and launched an enterprise-grade professional assistant leveraging its open-source agent framework, NanoClaw.

articles.title: GitHub Breach: TeamPCP Steals 3,800 Repositories via VS Code Extension
articles.summary: The threat group TeamPCP compromised 3,800 GitHub repositories using a malicious VS Code extension and is currently offering the stolen data for sale on the dark web for $95,000.

articles.title: Texas, Florida top list of states reporting millions of dollars lost through crypto ATMs
articles.summary: Residents in Texas and Florida have reported significant financial losses due to scams involving cryptocurrency ATMs, where fraudsters guide victims through the process of transferring funds. These incidents highlight the increasing use of physical kiosks as a common vector for financial fraud.

articles.title: Drupal critical update to fix bug with high exploitation risk
articles.summary: Drupal has scheduled a critical core security release to address a vulnerability with a high risk of exploitation. The organization warns that threat actors may attempt to create exploits shortly after the patch is disclosed.

articles.title: Webworm Deploys EchoCreep and GraphWorm Backdoors Using Discord and MS Graph API
articles.summary: The China-aligned threat actor Webworm is utilizing custom EchoCreep and GraphWorm backdoors that leverage Discord and Microsoft Graph API for command-and-control communications against government targets.

articles.title: Verizon DBIR: AI Helped Hackers Exploit Vulnerabilities in 31% of Recent Breaches
articles.summary: The 2026 Verizon DBIR report highlights that software vulnerabilities have surpassed compromised passwords as the primary attack vector, with AI significantly accelerating the speed at which hackers exploit these flaws. This shift underscores a critical increase in the efficiency and frequency of automated exploitation campaigns.

articles.title: GitHub confirms being hacked by TeamPCP, says customer data unaffected
articles.summary: GitHub confirmed a security breach where hackers known as TeamPCP claimed to have stolen source code from the platform. The company stated that no customer data was compromised during the incident.

articles.title: Carding site B1ack’s Stash dumps 4.6 Million stolen cards for free
articles.summary: The dark web marketplace B1ack’s Stash has leaked 4.6 million stolen credit card records for free following a decision to suspend its seller operations. This mass release of financial data poses a significant risk of widespread payment fraud for the affected consumers.

articles.title: Senator presses CISA for answers about alleged GitHub repository leak
articles.summary: Senator Maggie Hassan has demanded an explanation from CISA regarding a reported data breach involving government contractor Nightwing, which was first exposed by journalist Brian Krebs. The inquiry seeks to understand the scope and implications of an alleged leak from a GitHub repository.

articles.title: Agent AI is Coming. Are You Ready?
articles.summary: Orchid Security's 2026 report reveals that unmanaged 'identity dark matter' now outweighs visible identity components, creating significant security risks for enterprises rapidly adopting Agent AI. This gap suggests organizations are unprepared for the identity management challenges posed by new AI deployments.

articles.title: FBI: $388 million lost in crypto ATM scams in 2026
articles.summary: The FBI reports that Americans lost over $388 million to cryptocurrency ATM scams in 2025, as criminals increasingly use these physical kiosks to facilitate fraudulent fund transfers. The agency warns of the growing exploitation of these machines due to their high visibility and accessibility in public locations.

articles.title: ArmorCode gives security teams AI workers for exposure and remediation
articles.summary: ArmorCode has launched Anya Agents, an AI-driven framework designed to automate security workflows including triage, vulnerability remediation, and compliance at enterprise scale. The platform utilizes a Context Risk Graph to convert security data into actionable tasks for automated AI workers.

articles.title: Novata uses AI to map risk across portfolios and supply chains
articles.summary: Novata has launched Risk Atlas, an AI-powered monitoring tool designed to help organizations aggregate, normalize, and prioritize risk signals across their portfolios and supply chains.

articles.title: Fake Word Phishing Reveals Enterprise Blind Spot in Trusted Remote Access Tools
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered a phishing campaign using fake Microsoft Word documents to exploit trusted remote access tools and bypass enterprise security. The attack highlights a significant blind spot in how organizations monitor and authorize legitimate administrative software.

articles.title: Exploit released for new PinTheft Arch Linux root escalation flaw
articles.summary: A public proof-of-concept exploit has been released for the PinTheft vulnerability, enabling local attackers to achieve root escalation on Arch Linux systems.

articles.title: TeamPCP breached GitHub’s internal codebase via poisoned VS Code extension
articles.summary: TeamPCP gained unauthorized access to GitHub's internal private repositories by utilizing a malicious VS Code extension. GitHub confirmed the breach, noting that the exfiltration was limited to internal source code and did not impact customer information.

articles.title: Typosquatting Is No Longer a User Problem. It's a Supply Chain Problem
articles.summary: Attackers are now leveraging AI-generated lookalike domains embedded within third-party scripts, shifting typosquatting from a user-based threat to a supply chain security risk. Current security stacks often fail to detect these obfuscated threats, necessitating more advanced monitoring techniques.

articles.title: GitHub says internal repos exfiltrated after poisoned VS Code extension attack
articles.summary: GitHub reported that unauthorized actors exfiltrated internal repositories after compromising developer accounts via a malicious VS Code extension. While the company stated that customer data remains secure, the incident has raised concerns regarding the extent of the unauthorized access.

articles.title: Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports on TamperedChef malware, which utilizes trojanized applications and malvertising tactics to deploy stealthy payloads. The analysis tracks these clusters through identified patterns in code and certificate reuse.

articles.title: Encryption Consulting launches CertSecure Manager v3.3 with zero-touch certificate renewals
articles.summary: Encryption Consulting released CertSecure Manager v3.3, an automated solution designed to prevent certificate-related outages and security vulnerabilities by enabling zero-touch certificate renewals. The update expands support to 11 certificate authorities to reduce human error and minimize downtime risks.

articles.title: Banana RAT Malware in Fake Invoices Hits Customers at 16 Brazilian Banks
articles.summary: The Banana RAT malware is targeting customers of 16 Brazilian banks by disguising itself as fake invoices and security updates to facilitate data theft and QR code fraud. This sophisticated campaign specifically aims to compromise financial information by tricking users into executing malicious files.

articles.title: Darwinium updates mobile SDKs to detect remote access scam activity
articles.summary: Darwinium has updated its mobile SDKs for Android and iOS to help financial institutions and digital businesses identify and block remote access scams and account farming operations. The update shifts focus from point-in-time authentication to continuous monitoring of active sessions.

articles.title: A malicious VS code extension just breached GitHub ‘s internal repositories
articles.summary: A malicious VS Code extension was used to exfiltrate approximately 3,800 internal GitHub repositories after being installed by an employee. The threat actor group TeamPCP has claimed responsibility and is demanding a $50,000 ransom.

articles.title: Microsoft provides mitigation for “YellowKey” BitLocker bypass flaw (CVE-2026-45585)
articles.summary: Microsoft has released mitigation steps for CVE-2026-45585, a BitLocker security feature bypass vulnerability known as 'YellowKey' that requires physical access to exploit. The company is currently working on a permanent patch for the flaw.

articles.title: London's police asked Big Tech for comms data over 700,000 times last year
articles.summary: London's Metropolitan Police requested communication data from major technology companies over 700,000 times in the past year, highlighting the significant scale of state surveillance. The disclosure, obtained via a Freedom of Information request, underscores growing concerns regarding data privacy and police access to user information.

articles.title: Microsoft Releases Mitigation for YellowKey BitLocker Bypass CVE-2026-45585 Exploit
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a mitigation for the YellowKey vulnerability (CVE-2026-45585), a zero-day flaw that allows attackers to bypass BitLocker security features on Windows systems.

articles.title: GitHub confirms breach of 3,800 repos via malicious VSCode extension
articles.summary: GitHub experienced a security breach affecting 3,800 internal repositories after an employee installed a malicious VS Code extension. The incident highlights the supply chain risks associated with third-party developer tool extensions.

articles.title: DirtyDecrypt: PoC Released for yet another Linux flaw
articles.summary: A proof-of-concept exploit has been released for DirtyDecrypt (CVE-2026-31635), a Linux kernel local privilege escalation vulnerability caused by a missing copy-on-write guard.

articles.title: Microsoft shares mitigation for YellowKey Windows zero-day
articles.summary: Microsoft has released mitigation guidance for a zero-day vulnerability in Windows BitLocker, known as YellowKey, which allows unauthorized access to encrypted drives.

articles.title: Communicating cyber risk in dollars boards understand
articles.summary: Nick Nieuwenhuis argues that cybersecurity failures stem from an over-reliance on technical controls and poor communication between security teams and boards. He advocates for moving away from qualitative heatmaps toward quantifying risk in financial terms to better align with business objectives.

articles.title: CVE Lite CLI: Open-source dependency vulnerability scanner
articles.summary: CVE Lite CLI is a new OWASP-incubated tool that shifts dependency vulnerability scanning for JavaScript and TypeScript projects directly into the developer's terminal. This allows for real-time identification of CVEs during the coding process rather than waiting for CI pipeline results.

articles.title: When your AI assistant has the keys to production
articles.summary: The integration of agentic AI into live infrastructure management creates significant security risks, specifically raising concerns about potential confused-deputy attacks where AI assistants could be manipulated to perform unauthorized actions. This shift towards autonomous remediation introduces vulnerabilities that necessitate a re-evaluation of current operational security practices.

articles.title: Alleged Huawei zero-day blamed for the 2025 Luxembourg telecom crash
articles.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Huawei enterprise routers caused a nationwide telecommunications outage in Luxembourg, disrupting critical services for over three hours. The incident highlights significant risks to national infrastructure posed by unpatched flaws in core networking equipment.

articles.title: Grafana GitHub Breach Exposes Source Code via TanStack npm Attack
articles.summary: Grafana Labs confirmed a security breach affecting its GitHub environment resulting from a supply chain attack via the TanStack npm package. While internal source code repositories were accessed, the company states that customer production systems remain unaffected.

articles.title: GitHub investigates internal repositories breach claimed by TeamPCP
articles.summary: GitHub is investigating a security breach where the hacker group TeamPCP allegedly gained unauthorized access to approximately 4,000 private internal repositories. The company is currently assessing the scope and potential impact of the incident.

articles.title: 7 hard truths security pros should know: 2026 DevOps Threats Report
articles.summary: The 2026 DevOps Threats Report by GitProtect highlights that trusted Git hosting platforms have become major targets for cybercriminals, urging organizations to adopt better security practices to protect their code. It emphasizes the need for proactive security measures to counter emerging threats, particularly those involving AI assistants.

articles.title: GitHub Investigating TeamPCP Claimed Breach of ~4,000 Internal Repositories
articles.summary: GitHub is investigating a potential breach after the threat actor TeamPCP claimed to have obtained and offered internal repository source code for sale. GitHub states there is currently no evidence that customer data outside of internal repositories has been compromised.

articles.title: CISA credential leak raises alarms, and Capitol Hill demands answers
articles.summary: A major credential leak discovered on a public GitHub repository has triggered congressional scrutiny and security concerns regarding CISA's internal data management. Security researchers identified the incident as a significant exposure, prompting urgent demands for accountability from Capitol Hill.

articles.title: Ukraine says Russia is deploying AI-powered malware on the battlefield
articles.summary: Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council reports that Russia has significantly scaled its use of AI in cyber operations, particularly in malware development and social engineering. This advancement is reportedly creating a widening capability gap that increasingly disadvantages cyber defenders.

articles.title: Max-severity flaw in ChromaDB for AI apps allows server hijacking
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in ChromaDB's Python FastAPI implementation enables unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code and hijack exposed servers.

articles.title: Microsoft shuts down illegal code-signing operation used by ransomware crims to mask their malware
articles.summary: Microsoft dismantled an illegal code-signing infrastructure that ransomware groups were using to bypass security filters by digitally signing malicious software. The operation impacted thousands of victims, including multiple systems within Microsoft's own environment.

articles.title: Cybercrime service disrupted for abusing Microsoft platform to sign malware
articles.summary: Microsoft has dismantled a malware-signing-as-a-service operation that exploited its legitimate code-signing infrastructure to validate malicious software for criminal syndicates. By disrupting this service, Microsoft has hindered the ability of ransomware groups to bypass security defenses using fraudulent certificates.

articles.title: Attackers hit vulnerabilities hard last year, making exploits the top entry point for breaches
articles.summary: Verizon's Data Breach Investigations Report reveals that exploited vulnerabilities have become the leading entry point for cyberattacks due to widespread failures in patching critical defects. This shift highlights a significant trend in attacker behavior, prioritizing the weaponization of known security gaps.

articles.title: AI Agent Security: Automating Workflow Without Creating Prompt Injection or Data Leak Risks
articles.summary: This article discusses the critical security considerations for AI agents, emphasizing the need for strict access controls to prevent prompt injection and data leakage. It highlights that increasing an agent's operational authority necessitates a corresponding increase in defensive security measures.

articles.title: Discord rolls out end-to-end encryption on voice, video calls
articles.summary: Discord has implemented default end-to-end encryption for all voice and video calls across its platform to enhance user privacy and communication security. This update ensures that call content remains inaccessible to unauthorized third parties.

articles.title: FBI: Americans lost over $388 million to scams using crypto ATMs in 2025
articles.summary: The FBI reported that Americans suffered over $388 million in financial losses during 2025 due to scams facilitated through cryptocurrency ATMs. These kiosks are increasingly being exploited by criminals as a primary method for illicit fund extraction.

articles.title: Microsoft Self-Service Password Reset abused in Azure data theft attacks
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting the legitimate Microsoft Self-Service Password Reset feature within Azure and Microsoft 365 environments to conduct unauthorized data theft. This technique utilizes native administrative tools to bypass traditional security detection methods.

articles.title: Drupal is rolling out an emergency security update on May 20. You cannot miss it
articles.summary: The Drupal Security Team has announced an emergency security update scheduled for release on May 20, requiring immediate attention from all site administrators. The nature of the announcement suggests the patch addresses a significant vulnerability.

articles.title: Huawei zero-day attack behind last year’s crash of Luxembourg's entire telecoms network
articles.summary: An unexplained zero-day vulnerability in Huawei equipment caused a widespread outage of Luxembourg's telecommunications network last year. Huawei has not publicly acknowledged the flaw, though there is no evidence of further incidents.

articles.title: Microsoft dismantled malware-signing network Fox Tempest
articles.summary: Microsoft has dismantled the Fox Tempest operation, a service that provided threat actors with the ability to sign malicious software using fraudulently obtained trusted certificates. This disruption prevents attackers from using signed artifacts to evade security detection mechanisms.

articles.title: America's top cyber-defense agency left a GitHub repo open with passwords, keys, tokens – and incredibly obvious filenames
articles.summary: CISA accidentally exposed sensitive credentials, including AWS keys and passwords, in a publicly accessible GitHub repository with poorly named files. This configuration error highlights a major lapse in security hygiene for a federal cybersecurity agency.

articles.summary: OpenAI employees' devices were compromised by malicious npm packages, leading to the theft of internal credentials. The incident highlights a supply chain attack involving poisoned packages that bypassed initial security measures.

articles.summary: Unit 42 reports on the evolution of the Gremlin stealer, which now employs advanced obfuscation, crypto clipping, and session hijacking to exfiltrate sensitive data. The malware is specifically noted for its ability to hide malicious code within resource files.

articles.title: Unpatched Microsoft Exchange Server vulnerability exploited (CVE-2026-42897)
articles.summary: Microsoft is warning of an actively exploited, unpatched critical XSS vulnerability (CVE-2026-42897) affecting on-premises versions of Microsoft Exchange Server. articles.title: Rocky Linux launches opt-in security repository for urgent fixes
articles.summary: Rocky Linux has introduced an optional, opt-in security repository designed to provide accelerated patches for urgent vulnerabilities before they are released by upstream providers. This feature allows administrators to prioritize security responsiveness while maintaining the distribution's core stability.

articles.title: Microsoft warns of Exchange zero-day flaw exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft has issued mitigations for a high-severity zero-day vulnerability in Exchange Server that enables attackers to execute arbitrary code via cross-site scripting against Outlook on the web users.

articles.summary: Keycard has launched a new platform feature that enables developers to implement scoped, session-based access controls for autonomous AI agents. articles.title: Deepfake detection is losing ground to generative models
articles.summary: Advancements in generative AI models are outpacing current deepfake detection methods, which struggle to maintain performance when analyzing content created by newer technologies. Researchers suggest that closing this capability gap will require a fundamental shift in how deepfakes are identified.

articles.title: The AI oversight paradox: Is the investment worth the cost of watching it?

articles.summary: Google researchers have identified that malicious actors are leveraging artificial intelligence to automate the creation of zero-day exploits, Android backdoors, and supply chain attacks. These activities specifically target code repositories like GitHub and PyPI, representing a significant shift in automated threat development.

articles.title: Cookie thieves caught stealing dev secrets via fake Claude Code installers
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are distributing malicious installers disguised as Claude Code tools to hijack session cookies and exfiltrate sensitive developer credentials. The campaign exploits advanced techniques, including a new IElevator2 COM interface, to bypass security controls.

articles.title: Texas sues Netflix over alleged data practices that create ‘surveillance machinery’ without user consent
articles.summary: The state of Texas has filed a lawsuit against Netflix, alleging the platform engages in unauthorized data harvesting and tracking practices while demanding changes to children's autoplay features. The legal action seeks to impose fines and restrict the company's data collection methods.

articles.title: iOS 26.5 is out, bringing encrypted RCS messaging to iPhone and Android users
articles.summary: Apple has introduced end-to-end encryption for RCS messaging between iPhone and Android devices in the iOS 26.5 beta update to enhance user privacy. This feature ensures that messages remain unreadable to unauthorized parties during transit.

articles.title: TeamPCP Compromises Checkmarx Jenkins AST Plugin Weeks After KICS Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: Checkmarx has identified a supply chain attack involving a malicious version of their Jenkins AST plugin published to the Jenkins Marketplace. Users are urged to verify their plugin version to ensure they are using the authorized release from December 17, 2025.

articles.title: Identity security firm SailPoint discloses GitHub repository breach
articles.summary: Identity security firm SailPoint experienced a data breach involving one of its GitHub repositories. The company confirmed that the incident has been contained and that no customer data was compromised.

articles.title: cPanel CVE-2026-41940 Under Active Exploitation to Deploy Filemanager Backdoor
articles.summary: Threat actor Mr_Rot13 is actively exploiting the critical CVE-2026-41940 vulnerability in cPanel and WHM to deploy the Filemanager backdoor. The flaw allows remote attackers to bypass authentication and gain elevated control over compromised systems.

articles.title: FCC pushes ban on security updates for foreign-made routers, drones to 2029
articles.summary: The FCC has extended the deadline for banning security updates on foreign-manufactured routers and drones from 2027 to 2029. This delay provides additional time for manufacturers to comply with new regulations aimed at mitigating potential foreign-based cyber risks.

articles.title: Zimperium Mobile App Response Agent helps security teams counter mobile attacks
articles.summary: Zimperium has introduced the Mobile App Response Agent as part of its Mobile App Protection Suite to accelerate the detection and mitigation of mobile application fraud and security threats. The tool aims to reduce incident response times for SOC and fraud teams from days to minutes.

articles.title: Anthropic’s bug-hunting Mythos was greatest marketing stunt ever, says cURL creator
articles.summary: The creator of cURL dismissed Anthropic's 'Mythos' bug-hunting event as a marketing stunt after the AI scanner identified only a single, low-severity vulnerability in the software. The critique highlights skepticism regarding the effectiveness of AI-driven security tools compared to manual auditing.

articles.title: Red Hat extends open source technology into space
articles.summary: Red Hat has successfully deployed Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.1 and container-optimized technologies to a micro-datacenter on the International Space Station. This collaboration aims to provide a hardened, consistent platform for AI-ready workloads in orbital environments.

articles.title: Hackers Used AI to Develop First Known Zero-Day 2FA Bypass for Mass Exploitation
articles.summary: Google has identified the first instance of an unknown threat actor using AI to develop a zero-day exploit designed to bypass two-factor authentication for mass-scale attacks. This event marks a significant milestone in the malicious application of AI for vulnerability discovery and exploit weaponization.

articles.title: Instructure confirms hackers used Canvas flaw to deface portals
articles.summary: Instructure confirmed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in the Canvas platform to deface login pages with extortion messages. The company has since addressed the flaw to prevent further unauthorized modifications.

articles.title: Poor security left hackers inside water company network for nearly two years
articles.summary: South Staffordshire Water was fined nearly £1 million by the UK's ICO after a phishing attack led to a 20-month security breach that compromised the personal data of over 633,000 individuals.

articles.title: BWH Hotels guests warned after reservation data checks out with cybercrooks
articles.summary: BWH Hotels has notified guests that their reservation data was exposed in a recent cybersecurity incident. Customers are being advised to remain vigilant against potential phishing attempts resulting from the data breach.

articles.title: Google warns artificial intelligence is accelerating cyberattacks and zero-day exploits
articles.summary: Google's latest threat intelligence report indicates that cybercriminals are increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence to automate attacks, develop zero-day exploits, and evade security defenses. This trend significantly scales the threat landscape by enhancing the efficiency and reach of malicious operations.

articles.title: Why Changing Passwords Doesn’t End an Active Directory Breach
articles.summary: Resetting passwords is often insufficient to eject attackers from an Active Directory environment because persistent access can be maintained through cached credentials and active Kerberos tickets. Organizations must employ additional remediation steps to ensure complete revocation of unauthorized access.

articles.title: Romanian Man Faces Up to 30 Years in US Prison Over Vishing Scams
articles.summary: A Romanian national named Gavril Sandu has been extradited to the U.S. to face a potential 30-year prison sentence for orchestrating a voice phishing and debit card fraud scheme. The case highlights ongoing international law enforcement efforts to prosecute cybercriminals involved in financial fraud.

articles.title: Google: Hackers used AI to develop zero-day exploit for web admin tool
articles.summary: Google researchers have identified a zero-day exploit targeting an open-source web administration tool that was likely developed with the assistance of artificial intelligence. This highlights a growing trend of threat actors leveraging AI to accelerate the creation of malicious software.

articles.title: Google researchers uncover criminal zero-day exploit likely built with AI
articles.summary: Google researchers identified a zero-day exploit likely developed with AI that bypasses two-factor authentication by exploiting a semantic logic error in a popular web administration tool. The vulnerability has been addressed through coordinated disclosure with the affected vendor.

articles.title: Google spotted an AI-developed zero-day before attackers could use it
articles.summary: Google security researchers successfully identified and preempted a zero-day exploit that was developed using AI before a cybercrime group could deploy it for financial gain.

articles.title: Alation AI Governance creates a system of record for AI oversight
articles.summary: Alation has launched Alation AI Governance, a platform designed to centralize AI compliance and oversight, addressing the difficulty enterprises face in documenting and managing rapidly deployed AI tools. The solution provides a system of record to streamline evidence collection for regulators and internal stakeholders.

articles.title: Linux developers weigh emergency “killswitch” for vulnerable kernel functions
articles.summary: Linux kernel developers are evaluating a proposed runtime 'killswitch' that would allow administrators to disable vulnerable kernel functions in response to critical security flaws. The proposal was prompted by the recent identification of long-standing privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

articles.title: UK water company allowed hackers to lurk undetected for nearly two years, regulator finds
articles.summary: South Staffordshire Water was fined £963,900 by the ICO after a Cl0p ransomware attack exposed the personal data of over 600,000 individuals due to undetected network infiltration lasting nearly two years.

articles.title: SailPoint Agentic Fabric expands identity governance to autonomous AI agents
articles.summary: SailPoint has launched 'SailPoint Agentic Fabric' to address security and governance gaps for autonomous AI agents and non-human identities within enterprise environments. The platform provides oversight and control for machine-speed processes that traditional identity management tools do not cover.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Rootkit, macOS Crypto Stealer, WebSocket Skimmers and More
articles.summary: This week's threat landscape highlights a persistent trend of supply chain attacks, cloud misconfigurations, and the exploitation of legacy vulnerabilities. Attackers continue to leverage outdated security flaws and compromised trusted downloads to gain unauthorized access.

articles.title: 9-Year-Old Dirty Frag Vulnerability Enables Root Access on Linux Systems
articles.summary: A long-standing nine-year-old vulnerability dubbed Dirty Frag in Linux systems allows attackers to achieve root-level escalation. The recent availability of public proof-of-concept exploit code significantly increases the risk of exploitation.

articles.title: Webinar this week: Prevention alone is not enough against modern attacks
articles.summary: This webinar highlights the necessity of integrating robust backup and recovery strategies alongside preventative security measures to mitigate the impact of sophisticated cyberattacks.

articles.title: Dirty Frag: Linux kernel hit by second major security flaw in two weeks
articles.summary: A critical security vulnerability known as 'Dirty Frag' has been discovered in the Linux kernel, allowing local users with basic accounts to gain full administrative privileges. This flaw resides in the same kernel component recently impacted by the 'Copy Fail' bug.

articles.title: Police take down relaunched criminal marketplace with 22,000 users, €3.6 million in revenue
articles.summary: German and Spanish authorities have dismantled a relaunched criminal marketplace, Crimenetwork, resulting in the arrest of its operator and the seizure of a platform with 22,000 users and €3.6 million in revenue.

articles.title: Checkmarx tackles another TeamPCP intrusion as Jenkins plugin sabotaged
articles.summary: Checkmarx identified a supply chain attack involving the sabotage of a Jenkins plugin by the threat actor group TeamPCP. The intrusion occurred on a weekend, targeting software engineers through malicious modifications.

articles.title: Lyrie.ai Joins First Batch of Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program
articles.summary: Lyrie.ai has been selected as part of the initial cohort for Anthropic’s new Cyber Verification Program, which aims to enhance security standards for AI-integrated systems.

articles.title: Your Purple Team Isn't Purple — It's Just Red and Blue in the Same Room
articles.summary: The article argues that many organizations fail to achieve true Purple Team collaboration due to inefficient internal processes and operational silos, despite having competent staff. It highlights how fragmented workflows and slow bureaucratic systems hinder effective threat detection and response.

articles.title: Crimenetwork returns after takedown, dismantled again by German authorities
articles.summary: German authorities successfully dismantled a resurrected version of the Crimenetwork cybercrime marketplace just months after its initial takedown. Despite the quick intervention, the site had already amassed over 22,000 users and 100 sellers.

articles.title: Instagram messaging encryption removed, and privacy advocates are pushing back
articles.summary: Instagram has discontinued end-to-end encryption for direct messages, granting the platform access to user media and communication content. Privacy advocates have criticized the move, prompting Instagram to advise users to archive their data.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Vercel GenAI to Mass-Produce Convincing Phishing Sites
articles.summary: Threat actors are leveraging Vercel's GenAI tools to generate highly realistic, brand-impersonating phishing pages at scale, increasing the risk of successful social engineering attacks. This technique exploits automated site creation to bypass traditional detection methods.

articles.title: The missing cybersecurity leader in small business
articles.summary: Small and medium-sized businesses are increasingly vulnerable to sophisticated threats like AI and quantum computing due to a lack of executive-level cybersecurity leadership. The article suggests that federal government intervention is necessary to provide the resources and incentives needed to bridge this expertise gap.

articles.title: The scam economy has found its AI upgrade
articles.summary: The F-Secure Scam Intelligence & Impacts Report 2026 highlights that AI is being increasingly utilized to enhance the effectiveness of scams, which remain a persistent threat across multiple communication channels. Younger consumers and users in the United States are currently reporting the highest levels of exposure to these automated deceptive tactics.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in BerriAI LiteLLM to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical vulnerability in BerriAI LiteLLM (CVE-2026-42208) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation.

articles.title: TrickMo Android banker adopts TON blockchain for covert comms
articles.summary: A new variant of the TrickMo Android banking malware is utilizing the TON blockchain for stealthy command-and-control communications to target users in Europe. This evolution represents an innovative shift in how attackers hide malicious traffic to evade traditional detection methods.

articles.title: Taiwan's train cyber-trauma reveals a global system that’s coming off the tracks
articles.summary: The headline discusses the growing cybersecurity threats facing global rail infrastructure, using Taiwan's recent incidents as a case study for systemic vulnerabilities. It highlights the urgent need for enhanced security measures in interconnected transportation systems.

articles.title: Fake OpenAI Privacy Filter Repo Hits #1 on Hugging Face, Draws 244K Downloads
articles.summary: A malicious actor impersonated an OpenAI model repository on Hugging Face to distribute a Rust-based information-stealing malware to Windows users. The deceptive project successfully gained popularity, reaching the platform's trending list and accumulating over 244,000 downloads.

articles.title: Instagram removed end-to-end encryption for DMs. What should users do?
articles.summary: Meta is removing end-to-end encryption for Instagram direct messages on May 8, 2026, granting the company access to user chats and prompting concerns regarding data privacy. Users are advised to download their message archives as privacy protections for their conversations are downgraded.

articles.title: Rustinel: Open-source endpoint detection for Windows and Linux
articles.summary: Rustinel is a new open-source endpoint detection agent designed to unify telemetry collection across Windows and Linux environments using a single codebase. It leverages ETW and eBPF to simplify security monitoring and normalization for cross-platform infrastructure.

articles.title: Review: Foundations of Cybersecurity, 2nd edition
articles.summary: The second edition of Jason Andress's 'Foundations of Cybersecurity' has been released, updating the textbook to include modern security domains like cloud computing, IoT, and AI.

articles.title: Security teams are turning to AI to survive alert overload
articles.summary: The World Economic Forum reports that 77% of organizations are adopting AI technologies to manage cybersecurity alert fatigue and improve defense mechanisms like phishing detection and incident response. This widespread integration marks a strategic shift in leveraging automation to support security teams against increasing threat volumes.

articles.title: Two US Men Jailed for Helping North Korean Hackers Infiltrate US Firms
articles.summary: Two US men were sentenced to 18 months in prison for facilitating the infiltration of American companies by North Korean hackers using remote laptop farms. The operation involved assisting illicit workers in bypassing corporate security measures to access sensitive corporate networks.
